name: rcore_app
description: Frappe compose template for the rokctapp docker product (composes an app named rcore)
_comment: The erpnext fork has landed: the erp SDK's frappe module lives at pay/erp/frappe and its nextjs half at pay/erp/nextjs (composed via the 'sdks' key below). Adding the erp frappe module to 'modules' here is a deliberate follow-up (dependency and doctype-collision review), not automatic.

modules.name: gateways
modules._comment: Replaces the retired 'pay' entry (../pay/payments/frappe no longer carries a frappe module or manifest.json): pay's payments/frappe content moved into the gateways and wallet modules, so this template mirrors rcore.json's wallet+gateways pair.

modules.name: crm
modules._comment: Core CRM slice (leads, deals, contacts, organizations, notes, tasks, call logs, statuses) ported from Frappenize/crm (frappe/crm fork) into the productivity SDK. Composing this module replaces installing the standalone frappe/crm app — a site must NOT have frappe/crm installed alongside rcore, since the doctype names (CRM Lead, CRM Deal, ...) are intentionally identical and would double-define. Existing sites need one 'bench execute rcore.patches.crm_seed_defaults.execute' to seed default statuses.

sdks.name: erp_sdk
sdks._comment: Read by the Next.js composer (core/utils/nextjs/sdk_composer.py) only — the frappe engine reads 'modules' above and ignores this key. The erp SDK's nextjs half (accounting + hrms app trees). A Next.js shell for this product commits just '.rokct/config/app_type' containing 'rokctapp' and composes this list.

sdks.name: crm_sdk
sdks._comment: The crm SDK's nextjs half (leads, deals, contacts, organizations, dashboard — the frontend of the crm frappe module above). Listed after erp_sdk because its manifest 'requires' names accounting action files erp_sdk installs (requires is a warn-only prerequisite check in sdk_installer_base.py's check_requires(), not an auto-install).

_sdks_comment: A future agent tier means adding agent_sdk (../agent/agent/nextjs) here — its manifest's 'requires' names host paths installed by erp_sdk (app/actions/handson/all/accounting/*, .../hrms/*) and by productivity_sdk (app/actions/handson/all/projects/*), so an agent-tier compose needs BOTH of those SDKs in this list as well. check_requires() only warns about missing prerequisites; nothing pulls an SDK in automatically.
